key_insight: Reliable priors—not allocation policies alone—drive test-time compute gains, favoring solvable, intermediate-difficulty inputs over the hardest cases.
engineering_relevance: For shared retry budgets, prioritize solvability estimates and reliable verification before replacing round-robin with adaptive allocation.
method: Compare difficulty-proportional allocation with an inverted-U static optimum.
Test Thompson Sampling using priors from a related model’s past runs on the same inputs.
Probe sensitivity to prior quality and verifier false acceptances.
evidence_signal: Across public math, code, and formal-proof samples, difficulty-proportional allocation captures at most 13% of oracle gain on hard workloads; prior-informed Thompson Sampling raises the hardest workload’s solved share from 14% to 27%.
watch_item: For tested policies, gains vanish around prior rank correlations of 0.3–0.55 and require verifier false acceptances to be rare relative to the pass rate.
paper_title: Give Up to Get More: Priors, Not Policies, Govern Test-Time Compute Allocation
